slides.0.title: Whisky
slides.0.subtitle: All called whisky: four countries, four sets of rules
slides.1.title: Scotland and Ireland
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Basic rules for Scotch
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Distilled in Scotland and matured in oak casks in Scotland for at least 3 years, bottled at no less than 40%; single malt means one distillery, 100% malted barley and pot stills
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Scotch regions
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Five protected regions: Highland, Lowland, Speyside, Campbeltown and Islay; Islay is famous for peat-smoked styles (peat is used to dry the malt), and Speyside has the densest concentration of distilleries
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Irish whiskey
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Matured in wooden casks on the island of Ireland for at least 3 years; single pot still uses a mix of malted and unmalted barley in pot stills, giving an oily texture and spice: a uniquely Irish style
slides.1.content: Scotch keywords: 3 years, 40%, single malt, five regions, peat.
slides.2.title: America and Japan
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Bourbon
slides.2.highlights.0.content: At least 51% corn, matured in new charred oak containers, distilled to no more than 80%, entered into the barrel at no more than 62.5% and bottled at least 40%; Straight Bourbon needs at least 2 years. New charred barrels give rich vanilla and caramel
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Tennessee
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Similar to Bourbon, but filtered through maple charcoal before barrelling (the Lincoln County Process) for a smoother palate
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Japanese whisky
slides.2.highlights.2.content: A 2021 standard from the Japan Spirits & Liqueurs Makers Association: to be called Japanese whisky it must use malt, be fermented and distilled in Japan, matured in Japan for at least 3 years and bottled in Japan (with a transition period); many earlier products used imported spirit
slides.2.content: Bourbon’s style comes from new charred barrels; the Japanese whisky story is about authenticity of origin.
